title: Cut the page's boxes only when they do not all fit, sharing the pane's rows

notes.author: Jack Roddy/42dfd115
notes.text: Design, filed 2026-10-09. The five-line cut is a floor, not a rule. The notes pane has R rows; the body and each top-level note ask for the rows their whole text takes, borders included. Give every box an equal share of R, with the gaps between boxes taken off first. A box that needs less than its share takes what it needs and the rest is shared again among the boxes that still want more, until nothing is left or everyone is whole. A box that needs more than its share is cut at its share, with "⋯ n more" under the text. A share never drops under five lines of text: when it would, the boxes stop shrinking and the pane scrolls as now. Never cut a box to hide a single line: "⋯ 1 more" costs the row the line would take, so show the line instead. Thread pages and the body's page show boxes whole as now, since they are one thread; this is the issue's page only. With two notes and fifty rows, each gets about twenty-four lines; with one six-line note among many, it shows all six.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/42dfd115
notes.text: Refined 2026-10-09, and this supersedes the note above: the fit test comes first. Lay the page out as today, five lines and a marker per box. If that is taller than the pane, so the page scrolls, keep it exactly so: five plus one for every box, no exceptions. Only if it fits with rows to spare are the spare rows shared among the cut boxes, equal shares, what a box does not need going back to the others, until the pane is full or every box is whole; the page never scrolls in that case. Open: whether a cut that hides one line should show the line instead while scrolling; as decided, it does not.
